question: 12 UNRWA employees were clearly involved in the terrorist attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023. How will the Commission respond to this in terms of its financial support to UNRWA? Does it plan to conduct an investigation and will the Commission check whether those involved ever received EU funds?

According to recent reports, 1 in 10 UNRWA employees has links to Hamas or Islamic Jihad. How does the Commission assess this, what conclusions does it draw from it, and what will it do to prevent UNRWA staff from being actively involved in similar terrorist attacks in the future?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.7.2024) The Commission has welcomed the United Nations’ Office for Internal Oversight Services investigation to shed light into the serious allegations against the United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) staff.

Furthermore, it has commended the United Nations (UN) for creating an independent review group led by former French Minister of Foreign Affairs1 to assess whether the Agency is doing everything within its power to ensure neutrality and respond to allegations of serious breaches. The Commission has engaged with UNRWA’s Commissioner-General and welcomed his commitment to tackle the serious issues at stake.
Letters outlining the way forward and the measures and procedures for the Commission’s conditional funding for UNRWA were exchanged on 1 and 6 March 2024.

The conditions for the disbursement of the first tranche were the following: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the Department of Internal Investigations and ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-to-date, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen Department of Internal Oversight Services (DIOS) and ethics office.

Disbursement of the second tranche was conditional on the following: the Agency ensures the screening and vetting system against relevant EU sanctions list in place; UNRWA provides a progress report on the state of implementation of the concept note on how to strengthen DIOS and ethics departments; an action plan is adopted by UNRWA to implement the recommendations of the UN Independent Review.

Following UNRWA’s fulfilment of the above conditions, the Commission processed the first tranche of EUR 50 million on 7 March 2024 and the second tranche of EUR 16 million on 31 May 2024, respectively, out of the EUR 82 million for UNRWA in 2024.
Disbursement of the third tranche of EUR 16 million is subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.
